<0>AI Elements</0> started at Vercel as a component library for the AI SDK. Its repository now says it will be deprecated at the end of November 2026 and replaced by <1>AI Elements from shadcn/ui</1>, a set of patterns you copy into your project with no package to install. This page covers both, because people searching for one usually find the other.
<0>Artifact</0>: an edit that can’t be applied fails with a reason and keeps the last good version, previews swap in without a white flash, and runtime errors come with a Fix it action.
<0>Chat Sidebar</0>: delete with undo, rename in place, chats that are still replying, and thousands of chats that open instantly.
<0>Chat Thread</0>, with the free <1>Message</1> and <2>Message scroller</2>

<0>Chat Thread</0>: failed replies offer Try again, stopped replies say so, and edits and retries become versions you can switch between. Your question pins to the top while the answer streams, and older history loads without the view jumping.
<0>HextaAI</0> puts every block together into a complete chat app you can open and try before you install anything.
<0>Markdown</0> and <1>Streaming</1>: replies never show half-typed syntax, and bursty chunks are revealed at a steady pace instead of stuttering.
<0>Prompt Input</0>: Enter never interrupts Japanese, Chinese or Korean input, uploads show progress and retry, messages typed during a reply wait in a queue, and drafts survive a reload. It is free.
<0>Tool Calls</0>: every AI SDK tool state has its own look, including approvals, with “Tell it what to do instead” to send a reason back to the model.

A chat looks simple until something goes wrong. The reply fails halfway. The person stops it, edits an earlier message or sends another one while the model is still writing. A tool needs approval in the middle of a stream. An upload fails, or the model sends half a table. AI Elements gives you the parts to build each of those, and leaves the decisions to you. Its own Message example, for instance, shows Retry as an action you connect to `regenerate()` yourself.

AI Elements gives you the pieces of an AI chat, such as a message, a prompt input and a tool call. HextaUI gives you the finished screens those pieces become, with the hard states already handled. This page compares them as of October 2026.

The components are free and MIT licensed. The AI blocks and full screens are HextaUI Pro, a single payment with every later block included. Prompt Input is free.

Use AI Elements when you want free building blocks and plan to design the screens and their failure states yourself. Use HextaUI when you want the chat thread, the composer, the tool calls and the settings pages already built, with errors, retries, stops and approvals worked out. Both put their source in your project and share the shadcn/ui theme tokens, so you can mix them.
